Although BRAF inhibitor monotherapy yields response rates >50% in BRAFV600-mutant melanoma, only ~5% with BRAFV600E colorectal cancer (CRC) respond. Preclinical studies suggest that lack of efficacy in BRAFV600E CRC is due to adaptive feedback reactivation of MAPK signaling, often mediated by EGFR. This clinical trial evaluated BRAF and EGFR inhibition with dabrafenib (D) + panitumumab (P) ± MEK inhibition with trametinib (T) to achieve greater MAPK suppression and improved efficacy in 142 patients with BRAFV600E CRC. Confirmed response rates for D+P, D+T+P, and T+P were 10%, 21%, and 0%, respectively.
